thread:
raj: Quick heads-up — I put together a rough proposal for decoupling the heavy bench from the fast acceptance path. Goal: make preflight checks cheap and deterministic while keeping deep bench coverage as an async job. Thoughts?

maria: Love this direction. Can you sketch the gates you want on the fast path vs async? :thinking:

raj: Sure. Fast path: schema + tokenizer sanity + lightweight perf smoke (hotpath latencies with golden inputs) + basic model signature (shapes, KV support flags). Should be <2s per model.

sam: And async path is the full microbench, golden-sample variance, quantized binary compatibility, peak throughput, long-sequence regression checks?

raj: Exactly. Async runs on dedicated bench fleet, produces a compatibility artifact that we store with the model descriptor. If async fails we mark the model as "degraded" and attach the failure reasons to the model entry.

jordan: How do we avoid surprising customers if async discovers a critical perf regression after model is live? Rollback? throttling?

maria: We should expose a policy on the model UI: "allow-hotpath-only" vs "block-serve-until-bench-passes". Default => allow hotpath with throttled traffic + telemetry flags enabled. Ops can flip stricter policy per org.

raj: Implementation sketch: add a Gate API that returns one of {pass-fast, pass-degraded, fail}. Fast-path uses that. Async bench posts back a GateAssertion object. Example Gate config snippet: 

```json
{
  "gates": [
    {"name": "tokenizer_check", "type": "sync", "timeout_ms": 2000},
    {"name": "hotpath_smoke", "type": "sync", "latency_p95_ms": 1200},
    {"name": "full_bench", "type": "async", "depends_on": ["hotpath_smoke"]}
  ],
  "servePolicy": "allow_hotpath_throttle"
}
```

sam: A few tradeoffs: sync checks must be extremely cheap and deterministic. If we push too much into sync we regress onboarding time. But if too permissive we risk regressions hitting customers.

maria: For deterministic sync checks, we should pin RNG seeds, use canonical tokenization, and a fixed tiny golden set. Also return machine-readable signals (e.g., had_kv_support:true) rather than heuristics.

ops-bot: Note: creating async bench jobs will add queue pressure on bench fleet. Suggest backpressure and admission scheduling based on org tier.

raj: Yep — proposed scheduling: immediate for paid tiers, queued with priority for free tiers, plus a TTL for the bench result (e.g., 30 days) after which we re-run if model is still pinned in prod.

jordan: How will we represent compatibility in model metadata? Need a simple surface for routing and fallback decisions.

raj: Plan: model descriptor gets tags: [kv_supported, int8_compat, longseq_safe, bench_status:pass|degraded|fail]. Router can fallback to compatible variant if bench_status!=pass and route policy requires it.

maria: One more thing — telemetry. Fast path should emit a lightweight 'admit_event' with rationale so we can audit escapes later. That helps debug when async fails later.

sam: Agreed. Also add automated regression alerts: if async bench shows >10% dev from golden for any critical metric, create an incident stub in incidents channel with model id and failing artifacts.

raj: Action items: 1) I'll write a tiny RFC with Gate API shape and default serve policies. 2) @sam can prototype the sync hotpath smoke harness (takes the golden inputs). 3) @maria will draft metadata tags and UI flags for org policy. 4) Ops to propose bench scheduling SLAs.

maria: Sounds good — ping me when RFC draft is ready, I can add UI mocks. :thumbsup:

sam: I'll start a spike for the smoke harness tomorrow.

ops-bot: bench-queue: Job queued (id=bench-1747659999-1) for async full_bench. ETA ~4h with current load.

raj: Nice — thanks. Let's keep the sync surface minimal. We can iterate on degraded signals once we have initial telemetry.
